holidays.name: National Zipper Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble zipper, which holds up your jeans, seals your jacket and has saved many people from embarrassing wardrobe malfunctions. Celebrate by giving your zippers a little wax, noticing every one you zip today, or just being glad you don't have to fasten rows of tiny buttons.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance with no known founder. It honors the zipper's invention story, which began with Whitcomb Judson's 'clasp locker' patent in 1893. Engineer Gideon Sundback then refined it into the modern zipper design in 1913.
holidays.funFact: The name 'zipper' came from the B.F. Goodrich company, which used it on rubber boots in the 1920s. People loved the zipping sound so much that the name stuck.

holidays.name: National Shrimp Scampi Day
holidays.description: A day for garlic, butter, lemon, white wine and plump shrimp sizzling in a pan, ideally served over pasta or with crusty bread for mopping up the sauce. It's a good excuse to feel like a fancy chef in about fifteen minutes.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food holiday of unclear origin. The dish itself is an Italian-American creation. Italian immigrants in the United States applied their scampi cooking style to the shrimp that were easy to find there.
holidays.funFact: In Italy, 'scampi' means a type of small lobster-like crustacean, not the garlic-butter sauce. In American restaurants, 'scampi' describes the cooking style, and 'shrimp scampi' is technically a bit redundant.

holidays.name: National Peace Rose Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate one of the world's best-loved garden flowers, the Peace rose. It has large, creamy-yellow blooms with blushing pink edges. Plant one, sniff one, or give a bouquet to someone you'd like to make peace with.
holidays.origin: The rose was bred in France by Francis Meilland shortly before World War II, and cuttings were smuggled abroad as the war began. It was officially named 'Peace' in the United States on April 29, 1945, as the war in Europe neared its end.
holidays.funFact: When the United Nations founding conference met in San Francisco in 1945, each delegate reportedly got a Peace rose with a note hoping it would inspire lasting peace.
